---
title: "Fit and predict"
description: "Fit a circular response and predict directions in radians."
---

In `y ~ ref + x:z`, `ref` and `x` are angles in radians. The term `x:z`
adds direction `x` with a finite nonnegative modifier `z`. This example
uses the previous movement direction and the direction toward a meadow.

```{r}
library(CircularRegression)
data(bison)

vars <- c("y.dir", "y.prec", "x.meadow", "z.meadow")
d <- na.omit(bison[seq_len(100), vars])
form <- y.dir ~ y.prec + x.meadow:z.meadow

ref <- select_reference_angle(form, d)
fit <- circular_regression(form, d, reference = c("name", ref$ref_name))
ref$ref_name
fit$fit_status
coef(fit)
predict(fit, newdata = d[1:3, ])
```

The default method uses `angular_two_step()` to initialize a homogeneous
fit from a consensus fit. Use `angular()` to fit the homogeneous model
directly, or `consensus()` to let concentration vary with resultant length.
Use `select_reference_angle()` in new scripts. `pick_reference_angle()`
is the older name.

[Full introduction](introduction-to-circular-regression.html).
